tei:div.tei:p: These leaflet amulets were mass-printed in the 19th and early 20th century. The kame’a (amulet) itself is attributed to Rabbi Moshe Teitelbaum (1759-1841). We are not certain which epidemic it was composed in response to although cholera and measles epidemics were endemic throughout the 19th century. Derivations of the formula here developed into the Birkat haBayit found suspended near doorways of many Jewish homes.
We are indebted to Jacobus Swart for his explanation of this ḳame’a as found in his The Book of Seals & Amulets (Sangreal Sodality Press 2014). Thank you!
